To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nifL (nifA, nifL, nifA, ntrC) and nifH (nifA and nifA) promoters have conserved sequences that are required for efficient transcription and that the nifA and ntrC proteins activate transcription of these promoters with different efficiencies and different responses to mutations in these conserved sequences.
the conserved nucleotidesequences of the nitrogen-fixation promoters are required for transcription and that nifA and nifL promoter activation is differentially sensitive to base changes.
the nifL gene product is a negative regulator of nitrogen fixation and that it functions by repressing the nifH and nifD promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of conserved sequences and specific upstream sequences in the nifL, nifH promoters, and their regulation by nifA and ntrC.
the role of conserved promoter elements in transcriptional control of nitrogen fixation.
the regulation of nitrogen fixation in Klebsiella.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nifL (and nifH) promoters are regulated by nifA and ntrC, and that the nifA product has a higher affinity for the nifH than for the nifL promoters.
conserved sequences are required for nitrogen fixation promoter function, and that nifA and ntrC activation are not equivalent.
conserved nucleotid sequences are required for efficient transcription of nif genes, and that the nifL, nifH promoters differ in the degree of their response to base changes in these sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nifL (but not nifH) promoter is a good model for the analysis of nitrogen-fixation promoter structure and that the conserved sequences are required for efficient transcription of the promoters.
the Klebsiellapneumoniae nifH and nifL promoters have similar sequences in their -12, -14, -24, and -26 positions, and that these sequences are important in promoter function.

the conserved nucleotidess in nif promoters play a critical role in the regulation of transcription by the NifA protein, and that the conserved -24/-12 region is also involved in the regulation of the nif promoters by the NtrC product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Klebsiellae nifL and the nifH promoters differ in their response to base changes in the conserved nucleotid sequences.
the nifL, nifH, and nifA genes are not all regulated by the same mechanism.
the nifL, nifH, and fixJ promoters have different requirements for activation and that these differences can be explained by the presence of different upstream sequences in the promoters.
